markdown_report:
At 10% progress, prioritize a small, controlled extension: **GRU4Rec with a gated recent-window representation**, trained under a fixed BPR-max configuration. No new experimental results are claimed.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Recency weighting changes supervision rather than inference context. It cannot directly expose several recent items to the readout. (2) The previous latest-item residual offers a simple mechanism for current-interest specificity. Its main risk is replacing useful recurrent context with frequent item transitions. (3) Electronics has 22.31% small sampled margins and 9.01% negative-over-positive rankings. These motivate discrimination improvements but do not establish validation performance.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [Recformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13731) motivates recommendation-specific textual representations. Its pretraining and Transformer results do not establish benefits for this constrained GRU experiment. (2) [GRU-D](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-018-24271-9) demonstrates learned temporal decay in clinical sequences. Timestamp-dependent forgetting remains a separate recommendation hypothesis. (3) The [augmentation component study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.11136) motivates matched controls. An architectural gain must be separated from changing loss, sampling or regularization.

The framework separates three directions:

| Direction | Intervention | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|
| Supervision | Fixed BPR-max; optional target-age weighting | Current context remains implicit |
| Context | Gated recent-window representation | Recent activity may still be irrelevant |
| Item specificity | Joint title/description encoder | Semantic similarity can favor substitutes |

Three candidate ideas follow. Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Recent-window gate | 3/6/7/6/3 | Small change targets stale interests and broad affinity while retaining recurrent context | Extends the previous residual incrementally; benefit is unproven |
| Joint title/description pooling | 4/6/6/6/6 | May distinguish sparse item variants using available text | Adds preprocessing and can amplify substitute recommendations |
| Dropout consistency auxiliary loss | 3/5/4/6/5 | May stabilize ambiguous representations without extra inputs | User-facing relevance is indirect; two passes increase cost |

**Selected algorithm.** At each position, average the last four nonpadding input embeddings and project the result into the GRU scoring space. A learned scalar gate blends this representation with the corrected GRU features. Multiple recent events may express current preference more reliably than the latest event alone; this explicitly targets stale-interest ranking and broad historical affinity displacing specific recent matches. Fixed BPR-max targets weak sampled separation. These are hypotheses, not evidence of compatibility or complementary usefulness.

Compare ungated and gated models with identical windows, negative IDs, initialization of shared parameters, optimizer and loss. Track common sampled margins and earlier-history sensitivity; retain simulator judgments about immediate choice, stale interests and duplication separately. Select only through pinned macro validation HR@10. Keep one jointly trained GRU checkpoint per category, all four routes, and matching predictor export.

idea.description: Extend the supplied corrected GRU4Rec with a scalar-gated, causal mean of the four most recent real input embeddings. Train this internal feature path jointly with the GRU under an established BPR-max configuration. Each category retains exactly one independently trained network and one selected checkpoint.
idea.motivation: The recent-window path explicitly targets two user-observed failures: older interests outranking recent preferences, and broad historical affinity displacing specific recent matches. Pooling several recent events tests whether repeated recent evidence improves on the prior latest-item residual. BPR-max addresses weak sampled discrimination, especially Electronics' measured 22.31% small-margin rate and 9.01% wrong-rank rate. Neither intervention establishes current intent, ownership satisfaction, compatibility or complementary benefit.
idea.implementation_notes:
This is an integration proposal, not a standalone replacement train.py: the corrected baseline source is absent from the prompt. Preserve its GRU backbone, padding-invariant recurrent updates, input transformations, scoring activation, sampler, reducer and empty-history behavior. Insert the module after the existing feature transformation, using the exact transformed embeddings already supplied to the GRU. Do not introduce a separate embedding lookup with another dropout draw. The local pool uses only current and earlier observed inputs, never positive targets. Initialize shared baseline tensors identically across comparisons; initialize added modules separately and record remaining randomness differences.

First establish an affordable unweighted BPR-max control, then change only the readout. If the baseline uses one negative, expanding to a modest pool such as K=32 is a separate sampler/loss intervention; do not attribute its effect to the readout. Preserve candidate exclusions, duplicate handling, scoring activation, epsilon convention and baseline reduction across the readout comparison. Compute one global negative softmax without detaching its weights. Declare the BPR-max score penalty separately from optimizer weight decay. Do not add recency weighting simultaneously. A later latest-item versus four-item comparison is optional and consumes budget; never combine their predictions.

The proposed module pools recent item representations, not separately fitted transition or popularity scores. A learned projection and gate belong to the same trained network. The gate may learn a shortcut or suppress useful long-term preferences; measure earlier-history sensitivity while preserving the recent window and report this as a distribution-shift probe. Inspect common diagnostic margins, score norms and feature effective rank before interpreting directional embedding alignment as collapse. No embedding penalty is justified solely by the reported alignment score.

Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, single-GPU execution, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch, and the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget including diagnostics and failed trials. DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; all artifacts remain beneath the trial directory. Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl. Follow the host checkpoint rule and select only using its pinned macro validation HR@10; retain category results and all attempted conditions. No test access, external data, pretrained weights, other-trial checkpoints or claims of seed robustness.

Keep log2feats(sequence) returning aligned B x L features, item_emb and predict_score(features, items), family-specific sample_batch and every ModelView field. view.model remains the actual trained nn.Module. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). The diagnostic loader remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), each B x L. Mask diagnostic positions with zero input, positive or negative IDs; retain eps=0.5 and null item-category breakdowns. Only histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps are available. Preserve twenty training-user full-catalog recommendation probes and distinguish immediate-choice endorsements from broad interest, deferral and unidentified content.

Update the predictor writer with the complete module definition, window size, dimensions, parameters and unchanged scoring transformation. Export exactly one checkpoint per category with all routing preserved. Read the maximum nonpadding position rather than count-1. Verify causal pooling on left-padded and singleton rows, zero padding outputs, empty-history policy, g=0 equivalence, and training/export agreement. These checks and all performance improvements remain proposed, not executed.
idea.pseudocode:
import torch
from torch import nn


class RecentWindowReadout(nn.Module):
    """Internal jointly trained module; keep the corrected GRU encoder."""
    def __init__(self, item_dim, feature_dim, window=4):
        super().__init__()
        if window < 1:
            raise ValueError('window must be positive')
        self.window = window
        self.project = nn.Linear(item_dim, feature_dim, bias=False)
        self.gate = nn.Linear(feature_dim + item_dim, 1)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.gate.weight)
        nn.init.constant_(self.gate.bias, -4.0)
        # Initialize project using the supplied baseline policy.
        # Initialize this module without changing shared baseline tensors.

    def forward(self, gru_features, input_embeddings, sequence,
                fixed_gate=None):
        # input_embeddings are the EXACT embeddings used by the encoder.
        # Handles left padding; also skips zero IDs if gaps are present.
        valid = sequence.ne(0)
        batch, length = sequence.shape
        total = input_embeddings.new_zeros(
            batch, input_embeddings.shape[-1])
        recent_values = []
        recent_valid = []
        pooled_steps = []
        for t in range(length):
            current_valid = valid[:, t]
            current = input_embeddings[:, t].masked_fill(
                ~current_valid[:, None], 0.0)
            # Per-row queue advances only on a real observed item.
            if not recent_values:
                recent_values = [torch.zeros_like(total)
                                 for _ in range(self.window)]
                recent_valid = [torch.zeros_like(current_valid)
                                for _ in range(self.window)]
            next_values = recent_values[1:] + [current]
            next_valid = recent_valid[1:] + [current_valid]
            recent_values = [torch.where(current_valid[:, None], n, o)
                             for n, o in zip(next_values, recent_values)]
            recent_valid = [torch.where(current_valid, n, o)
                            for n, o in zip(next_valid, recent_valid)]
            count = torch.stack(recent_valid).sum(0).clamp_min(1)
            pooled = torch.stack(recent_values).sum(0) / count[:, None]
            pooled_steps.append(pooled)
        if length == 0:
            return gru_features
        pooled = torch.stack(pooled_steps, dim=1)
        recent = self.project(pooled)
        gate = (torch.sigmoid(self.gate(torch.cat(
                    [gru_features, pooled], dim=-1)))
                if fixed_gate is None else float(fixed_gate))
        features = (1.0 - gate) * gru_features + gate * recent
        return features.masked_fill(~valid[..., None], 0.0)


def final_nonpadding_features(features, sequence):
    if sequence.shape[1] == 0:
        return features.new_zeros((sequence.shape[0], features.shape[-1]))
    positions = torch.arange(sequence.shape[1], device=sequence.device)
    last = positions[None, :].expand_as(sequence).masked_fill(
        sequence.eq(0), -1).amax(dim=1)
    output = features[torch.arange(sequence.shape[0],
                                  device=sequence.device),
                      last.clamp_min(0)]
    return output.masked_fill(last.lt(0)[:, None], 0.0)


# Integration:
# base_features, actual_input_embeddings = corrected_host_encoder(sequence)
# features = recent_readout(base_features, actual_input_embeddings, sequence)
# Score with the unchanged host scoring transformation.
# Train under the fixed BPR-max control and original reduction.
# Preserve BxL diagnostic outputs and the original empty-history policy.
# Mirror this module/configuration in the embedded predictor writer.
# Select and load one joint GRU checkpoint per category; never fuse trials.

originality.positive: Tests whether several recent observations improve the prior single-item residual through a minimal, diagnosis-motivated change.
originality.negative: Local pooling and gated feature blending are established techniques; this is an incremental extension rather than a new model class.

future_potential.positive: A controlled result could motivate adaptive context lengths or elapsed-time-aware pooling while preserving the GRU family.
future_potential.negative: Recent-window similarity may still promote substitutes or irrelevant transitions and cannot establish compatibility or satisfied needs.

code_difficulty.positive: Adds one projection, one scalar gate and causal pooling without new data or independently trained components.
code_difficulty.negative: Exact baseline integration, matched randomness, padding behavior and predictor consistency still require careful verification.

related_work.title: Recformer
contributions: Motivates recommendation-specific learning from textual item attributes.
limitations: Its pretraining and Transformer architecture do not validate a randomly initialized GRU text encoder or the selected recent-window module.

related_work.title: GRU-D
contributions: Provides a recurrent precedent for learned elapsed-time-dependent hidden-state decay.
limitations: Evidence concerns clinical time series; recommendation improvements and intent-sensitive forgetting remain hypotheses.

related_work.title: Sequential recommendation augmentation component study
contributions: Motivates separating augmentation effects from contrastive-objective effects through controlled comparisons.
limitations: Does not directly establish gains for the supplied GRU4Rec backbone, recent-window readout or pinned Amazon evaluation.
